title: MindEval2: Clinically Grounded Patients and Rubrics for Evaluating Language Models in Mental Health Support
abstract: arXiv:2610.22314v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: With people increasingly turning to AI chatbots for mental health support, the need to evaluate these tools is becoming more pressing. Recent benchmarks attempt to mimic a realistic setting by simulating multi-turn interactions with synthetic patients and evaluating them with an LLM-as-a-judge. However, the usefulness of these methods is limited because simulated patients can be overly forthcoming and self-reflective, and judgments typically involve opaque Likert scales with unclear practical utility. To bridge these gaps, we introduce MindEval2, an evaluation framework that consists of two components: Mental Health Quality Rubrics (MHQR), for evaluation, and MindSim, for patient simulation. For MHQR, we collaborate with PhD-level psychologists to develop a set of rubrics that break down response quality into explicit operational criteria that are more interpretable and actionable than existing evaluation taxonomies. translated_title: MindEval2：基于临床实践的虚拟患者与评估量表，用于评估语言模型在心理健康支持中的表现
translated_abstract: 随着越来越多的人转向AI聊天机器人寻求心理健康支持，对这些工具进行评估的需求变得日益紧迫。近期的基准测试试图通过模拟与合成患者的多轮交互，并采用“大语言模型作为裁判”的方法进行评估，来还原真实场景。然而，这些方法的有效性有限，因为模拟患者往往过于坦率和自我反思，而评判通常采用不透明的李克特量表，其实际效用并不明确。为了弥补这些不足，我们提出了MindEval2，这是一个由两个组件构成的评估框架：用于评估的心理健康质量量表（MHQR），以及用于患者模拟的MindSim。在MHQR方面，我们与博士级别的心理学家合作，开发了一套量表，将回复质量分解为明确、可操作的标准，比现有的评估分类体系更具可解释性和可操作性。而MindSim则是（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出MindEval2评估框架，通过与博士级心理学家合作开发可解释、可操作的心理健康质量量表（MHQR）以及更真实贴近临床的患者模拟器（MindSim），解决了现有心理健康AI评估中模拟患者过于配合、评判标准不透明的两大缺陷。
en_tdlr: MindEval2 is a clinically grounded evaluation framework that combines Mental Health Quality Rubrics (MHQR), developed with PhD-level psychologists into interpretable and actionable criteria, with a more realistic patient simulator MindSim, addressing the limitations of overly forthcoming simulated patients and opaque Likert-scale judgments in existing mental health LLM benchmarks.
